The sound comes from the stick tips striking the note areas of the pan, not from plucking or bowing. The pitch depends on the size of the note area: the larger the oval, the lower the note; the length of the skirt corresponds to the treble or bass range. The order for a beginner is to become familiar with single-note strokes and the alternation of two sticks, and then to practise moving between note areas.
鋼鐵鼓屬體鳴樂器，發聲體由工業用鋼桶製成，現代琴身多用二百公升工業桶，早期亦見油: The steelpan is an idiophone; its sounding body is made from an industrial steel drum, a 200-litre industrial barrel in most modern instruments, while early ones also used oil drums, frying pans, dustbin lids and other metal containers. The pitch of the note areas relates to the length of the skirt: on treble pans most of the skirt is cut away, while bass pans keep a longer skirt. The sticks are straight with rubber-covered tips, in sizes and types that vary with the register of the pan; some players use four sticks. The surface is usually painted or chrome-plated, and may also be nickel-plated, powder-coated or hardened. The source does not state the materials of the other parts.
鋼鐵鼓常見於千里達嘉年華的打擊樂編制，由早期竹樂傳統演變而來。演奏時多用成對橡膠: The steelpan is common in the percussion line-up of Trinidad's carnival, having evolved from the earlier bamboo music tradition. It is usually played with a pair of rubber-tipped sticks, though some players use four. An all-steel band once performed at a British festival, and three steelpans were used on stage in the Broadway musical House of Flowers; other bands played at the Commonwealth Arts Festival and at the Montreal world's fair, and toured and recorded with Liberace. Its sounding class is idiophone, classification number 111.241.2.
鋼鐵鼓源自千里達與托巴哥，由二十世紀三、四十年代嘉年華竹筒樂（tamboo ba: The steelpan comes from Trinidad and Tobago and evolved from the carnival bamboo-stick music (tamboo bamboo) of the 1930s and 1940s, and further back from West African talking drums and the rhythmic traditions of the slave trade. In 1937 a percussion band of oil drums and other metal containers appeared in Laventille; in 1941 the stationing of the US Navy helped it spread. In 1951 an all-steel band played at a British festival and took the instrument international; in 1992 it was declared the national instrument, in 2023 the UN General Assembly set 11 August as World Steelpan Day, and in 2024 the parliament formally confirmed it.
鋼鐵鼓音色明亮溫暖，具有獨特的金屬質感。其音域寬廣，從低沉渾厚的低音到清脆嘹亮的: The steelpan's timbre is bright and warm, with a distinctive metallic quality. Its range is wide, from a deep, full bass to a ringing treble, and it has strong expressive power. When it is played, the surface of the pan resonates under the stroke and the sound waves spread through the hollow steel body, making a sound that carries well. Compared with a traditional bronze drum, the steelpan is softer and more beautiful; compared with a metallophone, its sound has more warmth and a more human texture. Its timbre combines the bite of percussion with the fullness of a harmony instrument, so it can show rhythmic tension and play a flowing melody; it suits many styles, and it is a unique and attractive instrument.
